This is a classic presentation of **chronic, localized bronchiectasis confined to the right middle lobe (RML)** — i.e., Right Middle Lobe Syndrome (RMLS). The focal auscultatory findings (crackles and wheeze *only* in the RML distribution) align precisely with anatomical localization — the RML’s long, narrow, vertically oriented bronchus with poor collateral ventilation and lymphatic drainage predisposes it to mucus stasis, recurrent infection, and progressive dilatation. - PFTs show ↓FVC and ↓FEV1 with normal FEV1/FVC ratio — consistent with restrictive physiology from chronic lobar atelectasis/fibrosis, not obstructive disease.

- Exclusion of active infection (no systemic toxicity, negative sputum for TB/fungi) — confirms chronicity, not acute infection.

- Serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level — pending; needed to definitively exclude A1AT deficiency, though atypical in presentation.
